_about.what: Centre lines of every modelled wire in rcc.glb (Radio Controlled Car), measured from the CAD, the servo plug, barrel plug and USB plug geometry, and each motor lead as a chain in its two CAD poses. Written by the wire-path study; see docs/research/rcc/cad_wire_paths.md.
_about.units: millimetres, assembly space of rcc.glb (Y up), as assembled
_about.conductors: Top-level keys NAUOn list the round conductors (swept tubes) found in that instance: solid = index in this file, mesh = the GLB mesh node, colour, radius_mm, length_mm (along the centre line), end_a / end_b = centres of the two flat end faces, points = centre line from end_a to end_b (2 mm apart or closer; chord error under 0.02 mm), check = distance of the tube's own vertices from that centre line (should equal the radius; the spread is the facets of the CAD tube). end_a is the end nearer the motor (or the battery clip). NAUO17 / NAUO18: the motors' three 1.5 mm lead stubs; NAUO15: the clip's two stubs; NAUO28 / NAUO29: the barrel plug's two stubs.
_about.chains: One entry per motor lead and pose: "NAUO17" / "NAUO18" = loose pose (right / left motor; plug NAUO21 / NAUO22), "NAUO17_plugged" / "NAUO18_plugged" = routed pose, plugged on U2 / U1 (plug NAUO19 / NAUO20). The CAD models one lead twice, at different lengths. Distances "at_mm" are along the middle conductor from leaves_servo_at.
_about.middle: The red (V) conductor from the inner end of the motor's stub, through the lead, to the point tools/wires.py plug() calls the middle top (1 mm inside the plug's cable-end face). The CAD's wires run 2.2 mm deeper into the housing than that (middle_trimmed_mm; conductors[...] keep the full CAD length); cut there, W.loose_lead() puts the loose plug exactly where the CAD has it (check_loose_lead) and W.plugged_lead() ends each wire on its contact top.
_about.across: Unit vector at the motor end from the brown (G) conductor to the yellow (S) one, so tools/wires.py ribbon(middle, across) returns [G, V, S] = [brown, red, yellow].
_about.lines: chains[...]["lines"] = {brown, red, yellow}: the same centre lines as chains[...]["conductors"][i]["points"], keyed by colour.
_about.G_V_S: Adapter-board headers U1 (x 717.50) and U2 (x 730.20): G at z 1318.43, V at 1320.97, S at 1323.51 (S towards the middle of the car).
_about.passes: chains[...].passes: every plate whose mid-plane the middle conductor crosses within the plate's outline: at_mm = where it crosses the middle of the plate thickness; in_thickness_from/to_mm = the stretch inside the plate thickness; conductors_at_mid_plane.tube_to_edge_mm = gap between that conductor's surface and the nearest cut edge.
_about.comes_near: chains[...].comes_near: every part (wood, battery, I/O module, adapter board, radio) whose surface comes within 2 mm of a conductor's surface, with the closest gap (negative = the CAD tube runs into the part).
_about.plug_position: plug_position = centre of the plug face that goes onto the header pins, as seated; plug_direction = the way the plug moves to seat (pins point the opposite way); plug_cable_end = centre of the opposite face, where the conductors enter.
_about.plugs: plugs[NAUO19..22] have what tools/wires.py plug(info, g_towards) needs (mating_direction, cable_end_face_centre, contacts[].centre) and g_towards, the direction to pass so that G comes out brown; w_plug = what plug() returns. plugs[NAUO28 / NAUO29] (barrel plug) and plugs[NAUO16] (USB Mini-B) have no three contacts: they give an axis, the tip and where the cable leaves instead.
_about.battery: battery: the battery lead's red and black conductors in both poses, from the clip to the barrel plug: battery[pose][colour] (pose "plugged" = NAUO41 + plug NAUO29, "out" = NAUO42 + plug NAUO28; colour "red" / "black") is the centre line, battery[pose]["conductors"][colour] the details.
_about.features: features: the holes and notches the motor leads pass through (L4's two lead holes, L1's two lead notches), outlines at mid-thickness.

seat.socket: USB Mini-B socket of the controller's Nano NAUO27

NAUO16.note: Only the Mini-B end is in the CAD (no A end, no USB cable on the car). NAUO16 includes 20 mm of the cable, straight along -x from the strain relief (cable_exit) to its cut end (cable_cad_end = cable_end_face_centre): a drawn cable that continues the model starts at cable_end_face_centre, leaving along cable_direction (as the MRA guide's USB_B_EXIT, 54 mm from the tip).

battery.about: The 9 V battery lead: two round conductors (r 0.7) from the battery clip NAUO15 to the barrel plug, in the CAD's two poses. Each conductor starts at the inner end of the clip's own lead stub (inside the clip, z 1347.68), leaves the clip's +z end at z 1353.68 and ends on the back face of the plug's grip. Red is the conductor from the clip stub at x 640.67, black the one from x 642.67 (Cadasio's colours for these sweeps; see colour_check). across = unit vector from black to red at the clip end, so tools/wires.py ribbon(middle, across, pitch=pitch_at_clip_mm, n=2, end_pitch=pitch_at_plug_mm, fan_mm=..., end_across=end_across) returns [black, red].

clip.on_battery: NAUO14, top at y 940.11 (the clip overlaps its terminals by 1.0 mm)

plugged.pose: plugged: barrel plug NAUO29 in the jack

battery.length_note: The two poses are one lead but the CAD draws it 32.7 / 30.5 mm long (red / black, clip stub end to plug) plugged and 26.8 / 25.4 mm out: the plugged pose is 5.8 mm longer (the plug moves 8.95 mm). A real 9 V clip lead is much longer than either: measure the kit's.

colour_check.about: Each conductor's colour here against the colour TechBox's Cadasio project gives the same solid: the length-weighted centre of our centre line against the Cadasio solid's centre of mass (raw/19075-rcc_remote_controlled_car.json, versionCentreOfMass, same assembly frame, mm). "nearest_cadasio_colour" must equal "colour".

stub_colour_rules.about: For materials.json: the order build_model.py's order_leads() puts each part's lead stubs in (mesh frame), with the colour each stub must have to match the leads here.
